method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, axiom-by-axiom reconstruction of all conjunction, disjunction and conditional claims, exact replay of the three-line modus-ponens derivation, and formula, macro, token, label and reference comparison after the documented OLAXD-004 and OLAXD-005 projections. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Basic propositional-connective consequences in axiomatic deduction: conjunction projections and introduction, disjunction inconsistency and introductions, modus ponens, and two sufficient premises for a conditional.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The section states that axiomatic derivability is strong enough to establish elementary propositional-connective facts, including conjunction projection and modus ponens, and that these facts are needed for completeness.
samples.checks: The proof system, derivability relation, both displayed examples, modus-ponens gloss and completeness role are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A conjunction derives each conjunct, while A and B together derive their conjunction. The first two results use the two corresponding projection axioms and modus ponens; the introduction result uses ax:land3 and two modus-ponens steps.
samples.checks: All three claims, both nested labels and all axiom references remain exact after OLAXD-004 replaces the duplicated second projection reference with ax:land2.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A-or-B together with not-A and not-B is inconsistent. The not-A and not-B hypotheses yield A-implies-falsity and B-implies-falsity via ax:lnot2 and the Deduction Theorem; ax:lor3 combines them, and another Deduction-Theorem use derives falsity from all three assumptions. Either disjunct separately derives the disjunction by the two introduction axioms.
samples.checks: Every negation, falsity formula, premise set, Deduction-Theorem step and disjunction axiom is preserved. OLAXD-005 corrects only the incompatible frozen ax:lnot1 citation to ax:lnot2.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A and A-implies-B derive B by the explicit three-line modus-ponens derivation. Not-A derives A-implies-B from ax:lnot2, and B derives A-implies-B from ax:lif1, with the Deduction Theorem used respectively as stated.
samples.checks: Both protected labels, all three conditional claims, the hypothesis order, line references, MP marker, two axiom references and the concluding respectively relation are preserved.

source_observations: OLAXD-004 records that the frozen conjunction proof repeats ax:land1 where the second projection uniquely requires ax:land2; the Marathi target corrects the identifier and carries an adjacent reader note.
OLAXD-005 records that the frozen disjunction proof cites ax:lnot1 for formulas that are direct ax:lnot2 instances; the Marathi target corrects the identifier and carries an adjacent reader note.
The frozen phrase modus ponsens contains a mechanical spelling error; idiomatic Marathi uses the established विध्यात्मक अनुमान term without creating a separate mathematical correction.
All formulas, macros, protected tokens, labels, identifiers and reference options match after the two documented reference projections.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
सिद्धतायोग्यता remains a definition-controlled formal compound under T184, and निगमन प्रमेय remains open to specialist review under T186.
The source gives compact axiom-reference proofs rather than spelling out every derivation line; the review reconstructed each cited schema and modus-ponens application.
